newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy president Thabo Mbeki's task group on communications is to propose sweeping changes to government information structures - including disbanding the South African Communications Service - while taking a pragmatic line on media ownership.
- The rand pierced the 4.50 to the dollar barrier on Thursday, threatening to burst the bubble of positive sentiment in the money and capital markets.
- Government revenue for the first five months of the fiscal year was surprisingly low, with the increase from last year running at less than four percent.

- Health director-general Olive Sishana might have to foot the 10.5 million rand bill for Sarafina 2 if parliament refused to recognise the spending as uanauthorised, it was argued in parliament on Thursday.

- Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and the National Union of Mineworkers have committed themselves to restructure mine operations to ensure increased productivity for survival into the 21st century.
- One of Telkom's most profitable businesses - international long distance business calls - is being snared by new operators, leading to major government concern.
- The Pharmaceutical Manufacturers' Association rebuffed charges by President Nelson Mandela that the local drug market was in the monopolistic grip of multinational companies.

- The commercial banks, who followed Standard Bank Investment Corp with a quarter of a percentage cut in prime lending rates, said they had not changed their view on interest rates, which they expected to remain high this year due to a continuing crunch in the money market.
- The revamped South African Revenue Services is set for a showdown with tax evaders, who deprived the South African government of more than 21 billion rand a year in lost revenue.

- Plessey Corp Ltd , the telecommunications and electronics company, will pay 20 million Australian dollars (72 million rand) for a 74 percent stake in the electronics division of AWA , a listed Australian company.
- The dramatic fall in copper prices after the Sumitomo affair earlier this year hit half-year earnings at Minorco, the Luxembourg based unit of Anglo American.
- Another furious Sarafina 2 row erupted in parliament amid new claims of a racial campaign against Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma and Public Protector Selby Baqwa.
- Iranian president Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and about 150 ministers, aides and Iranian media arrived at Johannesburg International Airport to a red-carpet welcome and a small, subdued crowd.
